items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.
Councillor Freeman offered further reflections on Truth and Reconciliation Day.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with moments of reflection.

items.title: This month is an opportunity to celebrate and recognize Islamic Heritage,
notes: specifically the contributions of Muslims in our community and across Canada.

Sharing the stories of individual and community achievement helps to ensure that members of the Muslim community see themselves represented in the fabric of our community. It is also an important way to interrupt harmful ideas that reinforce stereotypes and beliefs that lead to exclusion, discrimination and violence.
No one should be targeted because of who they identify as or appear to be.

As a Council, we recommit ourselves to confronting Islamophobia and hate in all forms. This work is not easy and it requires a long-term, continual effort. Working towards a community where all people, regardless of their identity, feel safe and included is worth the effort.

items.title: We invite everyone to join in a moment of silence to acknowledge and
notes: grieve the loss of innocent lives from the recent escalation of violence in the Middle East. This is a very challenging time, and there are many in the City of Waterloo, our friends and neighbours, who are feeling the impacts of this humanitarian crisis and who need our support. May we all find ways to express that support through empathy, understanding and a community- wide desire for an end to conflict. We reaffirm our commitment to standing against all instances of violence and hate. Shalom. Salaam. Peace.

items.title: Affordable Housing Commitment Motion – Councillor Bodaly
notes: Motion to be tabled October 16, 2023 for Council consideration October 30, 2023.
WHEREAS the City of Waterloo population increased by 15.7% between 2016 and 2021, faster than the provincial average of 5.8% and the national average of 5.2% during that same time period; and
WHEREAS the City of Waterloo’s population is forecasted to grow by 45% to 185,000 people by 2051; and
WHEREAS the City of Waterloo has committed to supporting the creation of 16,000 new housing units by 2031 as its Housing Pledge to the Province; and

WHEREAS the City of Waterloo approved an Affordable Housing Strategy in June 2023 with 81 actions, that, among other things, recommended ways to increase housing supply and the diversity of housing options, with an emphasis on areas near transit and transportation corridors.

WHEREAS the City of Waterloo currently permits up to three residential units per property as-of-right on a parcel of urban residential land; and WHEREAS the Government of Canada’s Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) grant program represents an opportunity for the City to review and accelerate actions to achieve more housing supply faster; and THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

1. That staff be directed to initiate an amendment to Zoning By-law 2018-050 to permit, as-of-right, up to four residential units and four storeys on residential parcels within low density residential zones, where appropriate (the “Amendment”) and report back to Council in Q1 2024;

2. As part of the Amendment, that staff be directed to identify appropriate zoning regulations and development criteria, considering matters such as safe access and servicing capacity, for Council’s consideration; and,

3. That Council confirm its support for the principle of intensification in transit supportive areas and near post-secondary institutions, and directs staff to identify opportunities to achieve the following planning objectives through the Official Plan Review, as recommended in the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy:
a. higher density housing options in areas supported by transit and near post secondary institutions; and

b. increase the supply of missing middle housing, evaluating opportunities for new missing middle corridors, modifications to the existing nodes and corridors strategy using a missing middle lens, and consideration of minimum height and density targets in specified areas to facilitate missing middle housing;

4. That Council reaffirm its commitment to our Affordable Housing Strategy, including the City of Waterloo’s goals to prioritize non- market housing, optimize existing housing, increase the supply of affordable housing, providing incentives to build new affordable housing, and enable a greater supply and mix of housing within our community.
5. That Council reaffirm its housing pledge of achieving the goal of 16,000 new homes by 2031, in partnership with the development industry.
6. That this motion be forwarded to the Hon. Sean Fraser, Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities of Canada for
consideration as part of our Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) grant application.

motions.item_title: Intimate Partner Violence Motion – Councillor Roe
motions.text: WHEREAS intimate partner violence, often referred to as domestic violence, means any form of harm caused by a current or former intimate partner or spouse in public or private spaces, as well as online, including actual or threatened physical or sexual force, emotional and/ or psychological abuse or harassing behaviour. Persons of any gender or sex can be victims of intimate partner violence; AND WHEREAS women are at greater risk of experiencing domestic violence including severe outcomes and femicide; AND WHEREAS on June 28, 2022, the jury in a Coroner's Inquest held on the deaths of Carol Culleton, Anastasia Kuzyk and Nathalie Warmerdam, who were murdered by a former intimate partner, issued 86 recommendations to the Province of Ontario aimed at acknowledging and combatting increasing levels of Intimate Partner Violence; AND WHEREAS every six days in Canada, a woman is killed by her intimate partner; AND WHEREAS in Ontario, 30 women were killed in a 30-week window between 2022 and 2023; AND WHEREAS intimate partner violence has been escalating in the City of Waterloo over the last decade where Waterloo Region Police Service have responded to 10,134 calls, or an average of 1013 calls per year, laying 5102 charges involving intimate partner violence, or an average of 510 per year, an increase of 109 percent; AND WHEREAS racialized women and Indigenous women experience disproportionately high rates of intimate partner violence; AND WHEREAS Indigenous women are approximately 3.5 times more likely to experience some form of intimate partner violence than non- Indigenous women and the femicide rate for Indigenous women and girls is approximately six times higher than for non-Indigenous women and girls, and Indigenous women are 12 times more likely to be murdered or missing than any other women in Canada and 16 times more likely than white women; AND WHEREAS 30 municipalities across Ontario have declared Intimate Partner Violence an epidemic; AND WHEREAS prevention and intervention strategies have been shown to help disrupt the cycle of intimate partner violence and protect victims from its effects; AND WHEREAS the City of Waterloo's Strategic Plan supports Intimate Partner Violence awareness as a stepping stone to shared wellbeing through the World Health Organization's Sustainable Development Goals, including: • Good Health and Wellbeing • Gender Equality • Reduced Inequalities; NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: THAT the City of Waterloo declares that intimate partner violence is an epidemic for all persons regardless of gender or sex, AND THAT the Province of Ontario be requested to declare intimate partner violence an epidemic; AND THAT the Province of Ontario provide additional funding aimed at preventing intimate partner violence; AND THAT the City of Waterloo continues to support the Region of Waterloo's Community Safety and Well-being Plan, AND THAT this resolution will be circulated to Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, Charmaine A. Williams, Associate Minister of Women's Social and Economic Opportunity of Ontario, Marci Ien, Minister for Women and Gender Equality and Youth, local area MP's and MPP's, and all local municipalities.
